To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) local binary features extracted by gentle boost decision trees can be combined with shallow neural networks to achieve fast and accurate facial expression recognition; (2) the proposed method is robust and can be used for within- and cross-subject facial expression recognition; and (3) the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance while being more than an order of magnitude faster than the state-of-the-art methods.
the combination of local binary features and neural network architecture is a promising approach to achieve high accuracy and fast execution times in facial expression recognition.
the proposed method achieves state-of-the-art recognition rates for facial expression recognition while achieving an order-of-magnitude reduction in computational complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a fast and accurate algorithm for real-time facial expression recognition that is suitable for embedded systems.
a fast facial expression recognition algorithm based on a novel combination of local binary features and neural networks.
developing a fast, accurate, and compact facial expression recognition system that can be deployed on resource-limited platforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LBF-NN achieves the best performance in both accuracy and speed, while maintaining the same level of accuracy as the best performing algorithm (LBP-SVM), but at a much faster execution speed.
our method is a very promising approach for real-time facial expression recognition.
the proposed algorithm (LBF- NN) achieves the state-of-the-art performance in facial expression recognition while being the fastest among all the state-of-theart algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an algorithm for fast facial expression recognition that is based on local binary features and a shallow neural network.
we present a new algorithm for facial expression recognition that is accurate, fast, and easy to implement.
LBF-NN is a fast and robust facial expression recognition algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple shallow neural network trained on local binary features can outperform more complex deep networks.
a simple shallow neural network architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in facial expression recognition when trained with highly discriminative features.

a simple neural network architecture trained on sparse local binary features can achieve state-of-the-art recognition rates in a fraction of the time required by the most recent deep learning architectures.
